classification.difficultyReason: Uses symmetry to separate the central coefficient from a full binomial sum and adjusts for the omitted initial term.

answer.short:
$\displaystyle \binom{2n}{1}+\binom{2n}{2}+\cdots+\binom{2n}{n}=2^{2n-1}-1+\frac{(2n)!}{2(n!)^2}$.

Use the full coefficient sum $2^{2n}$ and pair equal coefficients on either side of the middle term.
answer.worked:
Substituting $x=1$ into $(1+x)^{2n}$ gives
$$\begin{align*}\binom{2n}{0}+\binom{2n}{1}+\cdots+\binom{2n}{2n}&=2^{2n}.
\end{align*}$$
Let $S=\binom{2n}{1}+\binom{2n}{2}+\cdots+\binom{2n}{n}$ and $C=\binom{2n}{n}$. By symmetry, $\binom{2n}{r}=\binom{2n}{2n-r}$, so the terms strictly on either side of the middle term have equal sums. Each of these sums is $S-C+1$. Hence
$$\begin{align*}2(S-C+1)+C&=2^{2n},\\2S&=2^{2n}-2+C,\\S&=2^{2n-1}-1+\frac12\binom{2n}{n},\\S&=2^{2n-1}-1+\frac{(2n)!}{2(n!)^2}.
\end{align*}$$
